result.title: What Do Sparse Autoencoder Feature Discovery Scores Identify? From Activations to Interventions
result.summary: Sparse autoencoder (SAE) features are typically discovered from how their activations co-vary with behaviour, yet they are often used through interventions such as steering or ablation. We take intervention attribution, the first-order effect of a specified intervention on the model output, as our estimand. For a broad class of response functions, we show that observational feature-discovery evidence generally does not identify this attribution, and derive an exact gradient-based decomposition of the gap between linear-probe predictions and intervention attribution. Across four model-SAE pairs, median probe-to-attribution magnitude ratios range from tens to hundreds, while attributions closely track small-step steering. For single-latent ablations with nonzero effects, gradient predictions match the realized sign in 91-97% of cases, compared with 17-35% for probe-implied changes. Attribution-selected sets also produce larger absolute mean ablation effects on held-out prompts than sets selected by correlation, rank tests or probe coefficients. Together, these results establish intervention attribution as a principled, gradient-estimable target for selecting SAE features for intervention.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文研究 SAE 特征的发现分数（激活与行为的共变）能否识别干预效应，将「干预归因」定义为指定干预对模型输出的一阶效应，给出梯度分解解释线性探针预测与干预归因之间的差距，并在四组模型-SAE 上验证梯度预测在符号与幅度上更贴近真实干预效果。
AI.relevance_reason: 其中「观测相关性不等于因果贡献」的论证与梯度可估的归因目标，可供核查 LVR 中如何判断 latent 推理状态是否真被答案使用、以及视觉证据筛选与贡献分配的监督信号设计。
